title: Relentlessly Resourceful: the two-word recipe for a good startup founder
summary: Paul Graham distills what makes a good startup founder into two words: relentlessly resourceful. Relentlessness alone fails because startup difficulties are novel and of unknown hardness, so founders must keep trying new approaches. The quality can often be taught, and works as a self-test and a cofounder-selection test.

principles.text: A good founder is relentlessly resourceful: persistent, but constantly trying new approaches.
principles.quote: A couple days ago I finally got being a good startup founder down to two words: relentlessly resourceful.

principles.text: Pure relentlessness isn't enough because startup obstacles are novel and their difficulty is unknown in advance.
principles.quote: In any interesting domain, the difficulties will be novel. Which means you can't simply plow through them, because you don't know initially how hard they are

principles.text: The opposite of a good founder is hapless: passive, letting circumstances batter you instead of shaping them.
principles.quote: To be hapless is to be battered by circumstances — to let the world have its way with you, instead of having your way with the world.

principles.text: Resourcefulness can often be taught, especially to people who have always been under authority.
principles.quote: After four years of trying to teach it to people, I'd say that yes, surprisingly often it can. Not to everyone, but to many people.

principles.text: Use the phrase as a test for yourself and for potential cofounders.
principles.quote: If you want to know whether you're the right sort of person to start a startup, ask yourself whether you're relentlessly resourceful. And if you want to know whether to recruit someone as a cofounder, ask if they are.

principles.text: "Make something people want" is the destination; "be relentlessly resourceful" is how you get there.
principles.quote: "Make something people want" is the destination, but "Be relentlessly resourceful" is how you get there.
